beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) connection URI from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secrets store at runtime; never hard-code, commit, or log the full connection string.
Create a single MongoClient (or equivalent) per process and reuse it across threads/agents; do not create a new client per request. Close it cleanly on shutdown.

Configure sensible client timeouts and pool sizes: set serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS and maxPoolSize rather than relying on defaults; tune maxPoolSize for the agent concurrency level.
Use TLS/SSL with certificate verification for connections (tls=true / ssl=true) and reject insecure connections to the cluster.
Store database credentials and any LLM API keys in a secure secret store (Azure Key Vault or environment variables) and never commit them into code or seed files; load them at runtime.
Use least-privilege database users/roles for the app: a user that can read applicant docs and update score/explanation but not perform admin actions; avoid using admin/root credentials in the app.
When seeding data programmatically, use upsert semantics (replace_one or update_one with upsert=True) keyed on applicant_id to make the seed script idempotent and avoid duplicate documents.

Create indexes on all fields used in query filters or sort operations (e.g., applicant_id, status, created_at, score) and add compound indexes for frequent multi-field query patterns to avoid collection scans.

For vector search, create a vector index on the embedding field with appropriate index type and parameters (e.g., type: 'hnsw', similarity: 'cosine', m:16, efConstruction:200) and store embeddings as dense float arrays (float32).
Normalize embeddings (unit length) if using cosine similarity and store normalized vectors to ensure consistent distance computations for vector nearest-neighbor queries.

Combine vector indexes with scalar filters (push-down predicates) to pre-filter candidates by metadata (e.g., applicant status, region) instead of filtering only after vector search to reduce IO and latency.

Use explain() or the DocumentDB/MCP query plan inspection tools to verify that queries use the intended indexes and to check index usage statistics; remove or adjust indexes that are unused or cause high write overhead.
Avoid large skips for pagination; implement range-based or 'last_seen' pagination (e.g., _id or created_at > last_value) for predictable performance on large collections.

When writing score and explanation back into applicant documents, perform an atomic update (db.collection.update_one(filter, {'$set': {'score': ..., 'explanation': ..., 'score_history.<timestamp>': {...}}})) rather than read-modify-write multi-step operations to avoid races.

If concurrent updates are possible, implement optimistic concurrency (version field or last_modified timestamp in the update filter) to detect and handle write conflicts instead of silently overwriting.

Implement exponential backoff and bounded retries for transient network or server errors (e.g., network timeouts, transient server errors); do not retry on non-idempotent errors (duplicate-key, validation failures).
Set sensible operation-level timeouts for long-running queries (maxTimeMS) and for vector nearest-neighbor calls (if supported) to avoid blocking agents; surface timeout errors for graceful handling.

Limit document size (stay well below the 16MB MongoDB/document limit); store long explanations or large binary artifacts (LLM outputs, logs) in blob storage and reference them from the document if they may be large or grow over time.
Restrict network access to the DocumentDB cluster via firewall rules, VNet integration or trusted IP lists and run agents from known network ranges to reduce exposure.
Use least-privilege roles for any service principals or managed identities used by the app; prefer managed identities (if running in Azure) to avoid managing long-lived DB credentials.

Instrument and monitor important metrics (connection pool usage, operation latencies, CPU, RU consumption if applicable) and set alerts for error rates and slow queries; use explain() and profiler to find hotspots.

For test and CI, use a separate test database/collection or a dedicated test cluster and avoid running tests against production data; mock external LLM calls so tests run deterministically and without secrets.
Schedule regular backups (or use the provider's backup feature) and periodically test restores; for critical borrower data implement point-in-time or export-based backups.

When using LLMs to refine scores, treat the LLM output as advisory: persist the deterministic rule-based score alongside any LLM-adjusted score and store audit information (prompt, model, timestamp) for governance and reproducibility.
Use TTL indexes for ephemeral documents (session tokens, temporary caches) by adding an indexed expiry field and a TTL index to auto-delete stale docs and control storage growth.
